Given the information, I believe the best strategy is to rank the schools in order of my values: z > y > x > w. This is because even though z might be competitive, it's my highest value school and I have a reasonable priority ranking (2). If I don't get z, I'll move to y, which is my second-highest value school. If I don't get y, I'll move to x, and finally w.

Let's trace the algorithm. Round 1: I propose to z. Many others also propose to z. Given my priority of 2, I might be rejected. Round 2: I propose to y. Again, many others are proposing to y. Given my priority of 1, I have a good chance of getting accepted to y. If I don't, Round 3: I propose to x. And so on.
